title: Throwing a Ball on the Moon
learningObjectives: Calculate maximum height from vertical speed and gravity using ymax = V0^2/(2*g).
Explain that horizontal speed stays constant when nothing pushes sideways.
Explain that smaller Moon gravity makes the same throw rise higher than on Earth.

sources.title: Throwing a ball on the Moon (project-authored test text)
sources.attribution: Written by the Make knowledge interactive project team for testing.

evidence.quote: so a thrown ball feels no drag at all

explanations.text: On the airless Moon a thrown ball feels no drag and its flight is purely ballistic, with weight pulling straight down.

evidence.quote: so the horizontal speed stays U0 for the whole flight
Vertically, gravity slows the ball at a steady rate g.

explanations.text: With no sideways push the horizontal speed stays U0 for the whole flight, while gravity slows vertical motion at steady rate g.

evidence.quote: The ball stops rising when V = 0, which happens at t = V0 / g.
gives the highest point: ymax = V0^2 / (2 * g).

explanations.text: The ball stops rising when vertical speed is zero at t = V0/g, giving the highest point ymax = V0^2/(2*g).

high-arc - large vertical speed, Moon gravity

predictions.prompt: A ball is thrown on the Moon with horizontal speed 8 m/s and vertical speed 6 m/s. How high will it go?
